messages:
alex_g: thinking out loud — can we add automated nsys+perfetto captures into the perf CI job that only trigger on specific benchmarks? file sizes are the main worry but kernel timelines would help pinpoint selection/batching regressions.

maya-r: +1. we need lightweight captures for nightly (maybe sampling) and full captures for weekly or on-regression runs. also want KV cache trace points so we can correlate memcpy/kv-cache stalls.

tj: rough plan: put a capture step in perf-ci that runs a short scenario at target seq-lens (64, 512) and uses nsys for kernel timeline + perfetto for system-level. store artifacts to s3 under per-run path. e.g. s3://redwood-perf/ci/${BUILD_TS}/nsys.pb and .../perfetto.pb

kevin_s: to avoid huge outputs we can do: 
```
NSYS_DURATION=10s 
NSYS_FILTERS="cuda,cudnn,cublas" 
NSYS_CPUS=2
```
and a perfetto config with ring-buffer mode. keep the capture to first N steps.

maya-r: important: we should capture nvtx ranges from the runtime (kernel selector + batching hotpath). add NVTX_PUSH("kernel_select") and NVTX_PUSH("batch_apply") around those codepaths. that'll make post-analysis queries easy.

alex_g: good call — I'll open an internal CL to add nvtx markers and a small env flag PERF_TRACE=1 that CI can toggle.

lia: question — how do we diff traces across commits? we need an automated hotspot diff (kernel time per op) feeding into the perf dashboard. manual perfetto view is too slow for triage.

tj: proposed flow: nightly job collects traces -> post-process with a small parser that extracts kernel names, durations, and counts -> store a JSON summary artifact -> diff against baseline -> if regression > threshold, create a ticket and attach diff + trace links. we can reuse the existing diff-dashboard service (add a /perf endpoint).

ci-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/ci/1781234567/nsys-ci_1781234567.nsys (15MB) ; s3://redwood-perf/ci/1781234567/perfetto-ci_1781234567.pb (22MB) :white_check_mark:

kevin_s: for the parser, look at nsys export to csv: `nsys stats -F csv -o out.csv in.nsys` then run a small python that maps kernel name normalization (cuBlas->cublasGemmEx variants) and aggregates. I can proto that.

maya-r: also add kv-cache counters to summaries: hits, misses, avg-lookup-time. we can instrument runtime to emit a short telemetry file when PERF_TRACE=1. keep it tiny.

alex_g: next steps:
- (alex) add NVTX markers + PERF_TRACE flag in runtime (PR by EOD)
- (kevin) prototype nsys->summary parser and kernel-name normalization
- (tj) add perf-ci job config and s3 upload + API hook for diff-dashboard
- (maya) define regression thresholds (e.g., 10% increase in p90 kernel time or +50ms absolute)

kevin_s: timeline: proto in 2 days, parser tests using a couple of archived traces I have.

lia: can we redact any customer data from perfetto traces before upload? ci-bot: yes — CI runs on synthetic workloads and runtime will scrub identifiers when PERF_TRACE=1.

alex_g: one more note — kernel selection changes can show as many small kernel invocations instead of one fused kernel; the summary should include kernel invocation counts so we catch that pattern.

maya-r: agreed. please include both total kernel time and invocation count in the JSON summary. example summary keys: `kernel_name`, `total_time_ms`, `invocations`, `median_ms`, `p90_ms`.

tj: I'll add a small unit that compares `total_time_ms` by kernel between baseline and new -> highlight increases and new kernels. dashboard link (staging): https://perf-dashboard.internal.perf/staging/perf-diff?run=1781234567

alex_g: awesome. if we can get this working nightly it'll drastically cut time to root-cause perf regressions for batching/kv-cache changes. thanks all :thumbsup:
